references.text: Godliness leads to blessing and security, just as the midwives were blessed with homes because they feared God.
God promises to build a lasting house for those who are faithful to Him, just as He built houses for the midwives.
God promises to establish a house and a dynasty for those who serve Him faithfully.
By wisdom a house is built, and godliness is the beginning of wisdom that leads to blessing.
The Lord builds the house for those who fear Him and trust in Him.
Those who fear the Lord are blessed, and their houses will have abundance.
Moses' parents acted in faith and did not fear the king's command, just as the midwives feared God more than Pharaoh.
It illuminates the theological principle that the fear of God leads to concrete provision and blessing (both children and bread).
It illustrates God's fatherly mercy toward those who fear Him by giving them life and family.
A direct thematic parallel regarding God's ability to give children to those who fear Him or are in need.
It highlights God's intention that the fear of Him should be passed on to the next generation.
